records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages: uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 instead of Math.ceil, producing an empty phantom page that triggers a wasted fetch when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
records.rationale: The diff adds `totalPages: Math.floor(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit')) + 1` in admin-group.js.es6. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50), floor(2)+1 = 3 pages instead of 2, so `showingLast` (propertyEqual currentPage, totalPages) is false on the real last page; the `next` action then sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count)=100 and calls group.findMembers(), fetching an empty phantom page. Correct formula would be Math.ceil. Verified mechanism, real correctness defect.

If user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), totalPages = 3 but only 2 pages exist; `showingLast` (propertyEqual currentPage/totalPages) never becomes true on the real last page, and 'next' advances to an empty phantom page. Correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count/limit). This is a verifiable off-by-one defect introduced by the new pagination code in admin-group.js.es6.

records.issue_text: offset clamp in next (Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)) sets offset to user_count rather than the last full page boundary, producing inconsistent current-page display
records.rationale: The diff line `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))` clamps to user_count instead of the last page boundary. Combined with `totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit) + 1`, when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 with limit 50), next navigates from offset 50 to offset 100, which is an empty page yet reported as currentPage == totalPages — an off-by-one the correct clamp `user_count - (user_count % limit)` would avoid.
